title: Symfony Fundamentals
learning_outcomes: Explain what symfony fundamentals contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: project structure.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Frameworks provide conventions and reusable components for routing, dependency management, validation, persistence, and queues. Learn the underlying HTTP/security concepts first and verify the selected framework's supported versions. In this lesson, focus on project structure; then compare it with routing. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use symfony fundamentals when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Frameworks provide conventions and reusable components for routing, dependency management, validation, persistence, and queues. Learn the underlying HTTP/security concepts first and verify the selected framework's supported versions. For symfony fundamentals, begin with project structure. Also distinguish routing; controllers; services. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Use the smallest representative example, make expected behavior explicit, and test normal plus boundary inputs.

content_blocks.title: Walk through one example
content_blocks.text: Read the example for symfony fundamentals from top to bottom. Start by identifying project structure, write down the relevant variable values or control-flow choice, and predict the expected output before running it. Then change one input or condition, check a boundary case, and explain why the result changed.

content.task: Create a second small example for symfony fundamentals that demonstrates "project structure". Before running it, write down the expected result and one boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example includes a clear use of project structure.
The learner can explain its input, rule, and observable output.
At least one edge case is tested or documented.
hints: Start with the most direct listed subtopic and a single input.
Keep the example small enough that you can predict the output manually.
Test one normal case and one empty, invalid, or boundary case.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
